facts.fact: The Office of the Prime Minister's own IT Sub-Division states its core functions include developing systems, implementing and maintaining systems, systems administration, networking and maintaining ICT equipment for the Office; the document has no stated date, so its 2022 published year is used.

facts.fact: The OPM IT Sub-Division lists other offices, ministries and agencies (OMAs), state-owned enterprises, the Auditor General and regional councils and local authorities as external clients of its ICT services; the document has no stated date, so its 2022 published year is used.

facts.fact: The Electoral Commission of Namibia says its voter registration system is managed under its internal IT policies and that it has a fully-fledged IT Division entrusted with managing its IT systems.

note: States nothing on in-house IT capacity.

facts.fact: Namibia Business Review reports that the Namibia Revenue Agency launched its Onyofi customer service system on 17 November 2025, developed internally by its own application developer, with 1,443 registered officials and 11 service points.

facts.fact: Namibia's Home Affairs ministry executive director said the electronic visa and visa-on-arrival system was designed and developed in-house by ministry staff with no external cost.
facts.system: electronic visa and visa on arrival system

facts.fact: The ministry's in-house electronic visa on arrival system granted visas to 12,562 travellers who paid N$19 million in under a month, the executive director said.
